title: Hidden Coves Only Reachable by Boat on Thassos
excerpt: Discover secret lagoons, marble bays, and anchorages around Thassos that you can only reach when you rent a boat from New Port of Limenaria and explore on your own.
content:
Why explore Thassos from the water

Thassos hides entire bays unreachable by road. Rent A Boat Villy at New Port of Limenaria puts you in the skipper's seat — no guided tour, just your own hourly rental and the open Aegean.

A small speedboat unlocks turquoise shallows, sea caves, and quiet anchorages that beach buses never reach. You choose the stops, the pace, and how long you swim at each cove.

Departing from New Port of Limenaria

Limenaria sits on Thassos' south coast, minutes from Metalia Beach and Tripiti Cave. Most secret coves on the south and west shores lie within 20–45 minutes at cruising speed.

Arrive 20 minutes before your slot for ID check and safety briefing. Browse our boat fleet to match boat size to your group before you book online.

Half-day cove loop

A four-hour rental covers Metalia, sheltered pockets west of Tripiti, and a swim stop at Pefkari. Morning departures offer the calmest water and fewest other boats.

Preview distances on our sea atlas and compare hourly totals on the book online. Fuel is included on standard cruising around Thassos.

Paradise Cove and Kalogria Bay

Paradise Cove on the south-west coast is a favourite family anchor — shallow sand and clear water away from road crowds. Allow roughly 40 minutes from Limenaria in a 30HP boat.

Kalogria Bay catches golden-hour light on west-facing cliffs. Many guests plan a late-afternoon stop here before returning to the marina.

Anchoring safely

Drop anchor on sand in 3–6 metres, well clear of swimmers and rocky shallows. We cover technique during every briefing at New Port of Limenaria.

Watch for afternoon breeze on exposed north-shore coves. Ask our team for same-day wind advice before casting off on longer loops.

North-shore secrets

Small bays between Marble Beach and Vathi feel worlds from the resort strips. White cliffs and emerald water reward skippers who allow extra time for the north run.

Our Marble Cliffs track on the sea atlas shows the offshore GPS path from Limenaria. Plan at least five hours if Marble Beach is on your list.

What to bring

Pack reef-safe sunscreen, a dry bag, and water shoes for pebble beaches. On-board cooler space handles drinks and snacks for the day.

Mask and snorkel sets are available at the marina on request. Non-slip shoes help on the marina pontoon and when using the swim ladder on rocky coves.

Planning rental hours

Four hours suits a focused west-cove loop. Six hours opens the full southern-coast day with snorkelling and a lunch on board at anchor near Potos.

Use the book online to see live hourly totals. Peak season slots fill fast — request at least 48 hours ahead when possible.

Protect the coastline

Take all rubbish back to Limenaria. Avoid disturbing wildlife and never remove stones from archaeological zones such as Aliki.

title: Marble Beach by Boat — Saliara Anchoring Guide for Thassos
excerpt: White marble scree, emerald Aegean water, and the safest boat approach to Marble Beach on Thassos' north shore — timing, anchoring depth, and what to expect when you arrive by rental boat.
content:
Why Marble Beach from the sea

Marble Beach (Saliara) is one of the most dramatic stops on Thassos — white cliffs tumbling into deep green water. By rental boat you arrive before road traffic builds and anchor offshore for a private swim.

Rent A Boat Villy departs from New Port of Limenaria. You drive the boat yourself after a safety briefing — this is hourly self-drive rental, not a guided excursion.

The north-shore approach

From Limenaria, follow the offshore track north-east along the open coast. Allow roughly 90 minutes each way in a 30HP speedboat depending on conditions.

Our Marble Cliffs route on the sea atlas marks the recommended marine path. Stay 200–400 metres offshore until you identify the anchorage zone on sand.

Best time to arrive

Reach Marble Beach before 11:00 when north winds are lightest. Afternoon meltemi can make anchoring uncomfortable on this exposed shore.

June and September offer warm water with lighter crowds. In July and August, an early departure from Limenaria is essential.

Anchoring depth and position

Anchor in 4–6 metres on sand, keeping clear of swimmers and the marble scree slope. Set plenty of scope and watch your swing radius as other boats arrive.

We review local hazards during every briefing — submerged rocks near the shore and changing wind direction are the main concerns.

Photography from the water

The contrast between white marble and deep Aegean blue is extraordinary. Early morning side-light works best for photos from the boat or during a swim from the boat ladder.

Bring a dry bag for your phone or camera. Drones are popular here but check current local rules before flying near beaches and boats.

Combine with Aliki quarry

Pair Marble Beach with the ancient quarry at Aliki on the return leg — snorkel among submerged marble blocks after a calm lunch at anchor.

A full north-and-south loop needs six or more rental hours. Compare boat options on our boat fleet and totals on the book online.

What to pack

Water shoes protect feet on hot marble pebbles. Reef-safe sunscreen is essential — the white stone reflects intense sun.

Bring plenty of drinking water. There are no facilities at Saliara; everything you need for the stop comes from the boat.

boat choice

Any 30HP boat in our fleet handles the run comfortably. Smaller open boats suit couples; day cruisers offer shade for longer north-shore days.

No licence is required up to 30HP. book online your preferred date or ask at the marina about same-day availability in shoulder season.

Respect the site

Marble Beach is fragile and busy in peak season. Anchor responsibly, avoid crowding other boats, and take all litter back to New Port of Limenaria.

title: Aliki Ancient Quarry from the Sea — Thassos Boat Guide
excerpt: Circle 2,000-year-old marble workings and snorkel ruins visible only from a rental boat — history, anchoring, and the best self-drive approach to Aliki on Thassos' east coast.
content:
Aliki from the water

Aliki was one of antiquity's most important marble export harbours. Columns destined for temples across the Mediterranean left from this bay — ruins still visible above and below the surface.

The site is best appreciated by rental boat. You anchor offshore, snorkel the submerged blocks from the swim ladder, and view the peninsula coastline from the water.

Getting there from Limenaria

Allow 60–75 minutes eastbound along the south coast past Potos. Our southern-coast route on the sea atlas marks the marine path and suggested anchor zones.

Rent A Boat Villy rentals are self-drive — no guide on board. Briefing covers approach bearings and where to drop anchor safely. Guests stay on board — no leave the boating at Aliki or any stop.

Historical context

Quarrying at Aliki spanned centuries. Marble was loaded directly onto ancient ships from the twin harbours you still see from the boat.

Protected archaeological status means respectful behaviour — look, photograph, and snorkel from the ladder, but do not remove any stone or artefact.

Snorkelling the ruins

Submerged blocks and ancient cuttings lie in 2–4 metres of visibility-clear water. A mask reveals details invisible from the shore.

Mask and snorkel sets are available at New Port of Limenaria on request. Calm mornings offer the best underwater clarity. Swim only from the boat ladder.

Anchoring at Aliki

Use designated anchorage areas on sand, clear of swimming zones and archaeological markers. Depth is typically 3–5 metres.

Afternoon breeze can chop the bay — many skippers visit Aliki mid-morning on a full southern-coast day before returning via Potos.

Combine with Potos anchor

Potos lies west of Aliki — ideal for lunch on board at anchor near the harbour before or after the quarry stop.

Six rental hours fit Aliki, an offshore Potos anchor, and one west-coast cove on the return. Price the day on our book online.

Planning your rental

Any 30HP boat in our boat fleet handles the run. Families often prefer a day cruiser for shade during the longer eastbound leg.

Fuel is included for standard Thassos cruising. book online early in peak season when daily rentals sell out.

What to bring

Reef-safe sunscreen, water, packed lunch, and snacks for on-board meals. A dry bag keeps phones safe during snorkel stops from the swim ladder.

Underwater camera or phone housing rewards patient snorkellers — ancient cut marks are sharp and photogenic in clear water.

Respect the protected site

Aliki is a protected zone. Anchor only where indicated, stay out of roped archaeological areas, and leave no litter.

June and September balance warm water with lighter crowds. July and August demand an early marina departure.

Anchor on sand in 3–5 metres, well clear of swimmers and the cave entrance. Set scope for wind shift as other boats arrive.

title: Golden Beach by Boat — Chrisi Akti from New Port of Limenaria
excerpt: Reach Thassos' longest sandy beach by self-drive rental — east-coast routing, offshore anchoring at Chrisi Akti, timing for calm water, and how many hours to book from Limenaria.
content:
Golden Beach from the sea

Golden Beach (Chrisi Akti) stretches over two kilometres of soft sand on Thassos' east coast. By boat you skip inland traffic and anchor directly offshore for a swim from the boat ladder.

Rent A Boat Villy hourly rentals depart New Port of Limenaria — you are the skipper after a full safety briefing. Guests stay on board at all stops.

Head south past Potos then east along the open coast. Allow roughly 90 minutes each way in a 30HP speedboat depending on sea state.

Our Golden Beach Run track on the sea atlas follows the recommended offshore GPS path with distance and cruise-time notes.

When to go

June and September offer warm water with lighter beach crowds. In July and August, arrive before noon for easier anchoring offshore.

Morning departures from Limenaria beat afternoon chop on the longer eastbound leg.

Anchoring offshore

Drop anchor on sand beyond the swimming zone — typically 4–8 metres depending on tide and crowd. Watch for swimmers and pedal boats near the shore.

Set a stern anchor or bow anchor with adequate scope; east-coast breeze can build after midday. Swim and snorkel only from the swim ladder.

The Golden Beach Run route is priced as a five-hour minimum recommendation — three hours on site after the cruise each way.

Use the book online with five or six hours selected to see live totals for each boat on boat fleet.

An offshore anchor near Potos makes a natural lunch-on-board break on the outbound or return leg. View the harbour village from the water while you eat on deck.

What to pack

Long beach days need extra water, sun hats, packed lunch, and reef-safe sunscreen. A dry bag protects towels and electronics during swim-ladder stops.

Water shoes are optional on soft sand but useful on the marina pontoon and any pebble stops en route.

boat recommendations

title: Best Snorkelling in Thassos — Self-Drive Boat Stops from Limenaria

content:
Snorkel Thassos by rental boat

The best snorkelling on Thassos sits on shores you reach by boat — shallow ruins, iron-ore formations, and clear north-coast reefs. Rent A Boat Villy rentals are self-drive from New Port of Limenaria.

You choose the stops and duration. We provide briefing and optional mask sets — no guided snorkel tour, just your hourly boat rental and a map of marine highlights.

Metalia Beach near Limenaria

Iron-ore formations create interesting underwater terrain just south of the marina. Shallow, calm, and perfect for beginners on a first rental morning.

Pair Metalia with Tripiti on a four-hour loop — two distinct snorkel profiles within 30 minutes of Limenaria.

Depth and visibility

Expect 2–4 metres depth over mixed sand and rock. Morning light penetrates best before surface chop builds.

Anchor on sand and swim toward the ore-stained rocks — colourful wrasse and small octopus are common in summer.

Aliki submerged ruins

Ancient marble blocks lie in clear water 2–4 metres deep — one of the most unique snorkel sites in the Aegean. Reach Aliki on a six-hour southern-coast day.

Protected site rules apply: look but never remove stone. Our sea atlas marks approach and anchor zones.

Tripiti Cave area

Snorkel outside the cave mouth and along the pebble shore for dramatic underwater light. Calm mornings essential — afternoon swell reduces visibility.

Four hours from Limenaria covers Metalia, Tripiti snorkel, and swim time without rushing.

North-shore reefs

Marble Beach and bays toward Vathi offer clearer deep water for confident swimmers. Book longer hours and check wind before committing north.

Gear we provide

title: Southern Coast Boat Itinerary — Self-Drive Day from Limenaria

content:
The classic south-coast day

This itinerary is the most requested full-day loop for Rent A Boat Villy guests — west coves in the morning, lunch on board at anchor near Potos, then Aliki ruins before the return to New Port of Limenaria.

You drive the boat yourself on an hourly rental. Our Southern Coast Discovery track on the sea atlas mirrors this GPS path. Guests stay on board at all anchor stops — swimming only from the swim ladder.

Morning — west coves

Depart Limenaria at 09:30. First stop Metalia Beach for a snorkel in iron-ore shallows while the south-west wind is still light.

Continue to Tripiti Cave for photos and a swim from the boat ladder near the arch — aim to leave by 11:00 if continuing east.

Mid-morning timing

Allow 25 minutes between Metalia and Tripiti, then 20 minutes to Pefkari. Do not linger too long early if Aliki is on your afternoon plan.

Fuel is included on standard hourly rates — focus on time management rather than engine worry.

Midday — Pefkari and Potos

Anchor at Pefkari for a sandy swim from the ladder — shallow water ideal for families. Then cruise to an offshore anchor near Potos for lunch on board.

Pack your picnic before departure from New Port of Limenaria. Enjoy harbour and coastline views from the water while you eat on deck — no leave the boating at Potos or any beach.

Afternoon — Aliki quarry

Finish at Aliki Ancient Quarry for history and snorkelling among submerged marble blocks from the boat ladder. View the peninsula ruins from the water — stay on board throughout.

Depart Aliki by 16:30 for a comfortable Limenaria return. Total active time: six to seven rental hours. Use book online with six hours selected to compare boat totals.

Wind considerations

South-coast breeze often builds after 14:00. Eastbound legs to Aliki can feel choppier — secure loose items and plan a steady cruise speed.

If wind is strong, shorten to Metalia–Tripiti–Pefkari and skip Aliki — our team advises at morning briefing.

Boat choice

Any 30HP boat on boat fleet handles the loop. Day cruisers suit groups wanting shade on long open legs; open boats suit agile couples.

No licence required up to 30HP. Book six or seven hours in peak season — book online early.

Water, packed lunch, snacks, reef-safe sunscreen. Dry bag for phones during snorkel stops at Metalia and Aliki.

Water shoes help when using the swim ladder at Tripiti and Aliki anchorages.

Four hours: Metalia and Tripiti only. Five hours: add Pefkari without Aliki. Match hours to your group energy and weather.

Every waypoint on sea atlas shows cruise time from Limenaria for custom variants.

title: Boat Rental Safety at Limenaria — Stay On Board Policy
excerpt: Essential safety rules for self-drive boat rental at Rent A Boat Villy New Port of Limenaria — stay-on-board policy, briefing, life jackets, anchoring, weather, VHF, and why guests cannot leave the boat at beaches or harbours.
content:
Safety first at Rent A Boat Villy

Every hourly self-drive rental from New Port of Limenaria begins with safety. Rent A Boat Villy is a family-run operation — we want you to enjoy Thassos from the water and return to the marina without incident.

This guide explains our stay-on-board policy, what the briefing covers, and the habits that keep your boat rental day safe and fun.

Stay on board — no exceptions

Guests cannot disembark or be dropped off from the boat at beaches, harbours, or coves. You must stay on board throughout your rental. This is a firm policy driven by insurance requirements and passenger safety.

Swimming and snorkelling are permitted only from the swim ladder around your anchored boat. Enter and exit the water at the ladder — never swim to shore or climb onto beaches from the boat.

Lunch and all meals are enjoyed on board. Pack food and drinks in the on-board cooler before departure, or prepare snacks at New Port of Limenaria.

Why this policy exists

Self-drive rental boats are insured for on-board use and anchored swimming. Allowing guests ashore at multiple stops creates liability, grounding risk, and propeller hazards that we cannot accept.

The policy protects you, other swimmers, and our fleet. It also keeps your day simple — anchor, swim from the ladder, move to the next cove.

Pre-departure safety briefing

Arrive 20 minutes before your slot for ID check and a 15–20 minute briefing. We cover boat controls, kill switch, throttle, steering, anchor setup, and designated cruising areas around Thassos.

First-time skippers receive extra time on docking at the marina wall and anchor technique on sand. Ask every question — local knowledge prevents most first-day mistakes.

GPS tracks for popular routes are shared via our sea atlas. Browse our boat fleet before you book online to match boat size to your group.

Life jackets and onboard equipment

Life jackets for all guests are included on every departure. Children and non-swimmers should wear them whenever the boat is underway and consider wearing them at anchor in choppy conditions.

Each boat carries a kill switch lanyard, anchor with adequate chain and rope, navigation lights, fire extinguisher, bilge pump, and VHF radio where fitted. Briefing explains location and use of each item.

Swim ladder rules

Use the swim ladder to enter and exit the water. Never jump from the bow or stern near the propeller. Keep the engine off and kill switch engaged whenever anyone is in the water.

One person should remain on board to watch swimmers at all times. Never snorkel or swim alone — the buddy system applies at every anchor stop.

Anchor safety

Drop anchor on sand in 3–6 metres where briefing allows. Set adequate scope for wind shift and watch your swing radius as other boats arrive.

We review anchoring technique during every briefing — sand identification, scope ratio, and how to raise anchor cleanly before departure. Avoid rocky shallows and archaeological zones marked on the sea atlas.

If anchor drags, restart the engine, circle back, and re-set on sand. Do not attempt to beach the boat at any location.

Weather and go/no-go decisions

We monitor forecasts daily from New Port of Limenaria. If conditions are unsafe, we reschedule at no cost or refund your deposit in full.

Morning sea state is usually calmest on Thassos. South and west shores are more sheltered than exposed north-coast routes to Marble Beach and Vathi. Our team advises on same-day wind at check-in.

If breeze builds during your rental, shorten your loop and return early. Never push a north-shore plan when meltemi is forecast.

Propeller and engine rules

The propeller is the most dangerous part of any rental day. Engine off, kill switch on, and keys removed whenever passengers swim or snorkel.

Before starting the engine, confirm all guests are seated, nothing trails in the water, and the area around the stern is clear. Brief children on staying seated while underway.

VHF and communication

Briefing covers basic VHF use — channel 16 for emergency, working channels for marina contact. Our team monitors VHF during operating hours 08:00–20:00, May through October.

Mobile signal varies offshore. Note our marina contact number at check-in. In any doubt, call before attempting a difficult manoeuvre.

Navigation and cruising zones

Stay within designated cruising areas explained at briefing. Follow GPS tracks on the sea atlas — especially on north-coast cliff sections with submerged rocks.

Maintain safe speed near swimmers, anchored boats, and the marina entrance. No licence is required up to 30HP, but responsible speed is mandatory.

What to pack for a safe day

Reef-safe sunscreen, hats, non-slip shoes, plenty of water, packed lunch, and a dry bag for phones. Avoid glass bottles on board.

Mask and snorkel sets are available at the marina on request. Bring any prescription medications and a light jacket for breezy returns.

Book with confidence

Understanding the stay-on-board policy before boat rental day prevents disappointment. You still see Thassos' best coves, ruins, and coastline — all from the water, with swims from the ladder at each anchor.

Thassos in the North Aegean

Thassos is the northernmost major Greek island in the Aegean Sea — green, mountainous, and ringed by beaches and coves that reward exploration from the water. Unlike barren Cycladic islands, Thassos is covered in pine forests, olive groves, and ancient marble quarries.

For boat renters, the coastline is the main attraction. Road access reaches many beaches, but the quietest anchorages and dramatic sea caves are best reached by rental boat from New Port of Limenaria.

Geography and coastlines

Thassos is roughly circular, about 26 kilometres across. A mountain ridge runs east-west through the centre, dividing the island into distinct north and south shores.

The south coast faces the mainland — generally calmer, with sandy bays like Pefkari, Potos, and Golden Beach (Chrisi Akti). The south coast around Limenaria offers iron-ore cliffs at Metalia and sea caves at Tripiti.

The north coast is more exposed to meltemi wind but delivers Marble Beach (Saliara), white cliffs, and forest-backed bays like Vathi. Each shore has a different character — plan your rental day accordingly.

North vs south — which to choose

First-time renters and families should start on the south and west coasts — Metalia, Tripiti, Pefkari, and offshore anchors near Potos and Aliki. Calmer water and shorter distances from New Port of Limenaria.

Experienced skippers on calm mornings can attempt the north-shore Marble Route to Saliara and Kalogria. Check wind at briefing and allow five to six rental hours.

How to get to Thassos

Most visitors drive to Keramoti on the mainland and take the frequent ferry to Limenas (Thassos Town) — roughly 45 minutes. From Limenas, Limenaria is 40 minutes south by car or bus.

The nearest airport is Kavala (KVA) on the mainland, about 30 minutes from Keramoti ferry port. Thessaloniki airport is a longer but viable option for international flights.

Once on Thassos, Limenaria sits on the west coast — close to Metalia, Tripiti, and the southern-coast routes that Rent A Boat Villy guests use most.

Limenaria is a harbour town on Thassos' west coast with a working marina, tavernas on the waterfront, and easy parking. Rent A Boat Villy operates daily self-drive hourly rentals from New Port of Limenaria, May through October.

From here you reach Metalia Beach in 10–15 minutes, Tripiti Cave in 30 minutes, and the full southern-coast loop to Aliki in six to seven hours. No other base on Thassos offers this range of boat-accessible destinations so quickly.

Seasons and when to visit

Peak season is July and August — warmest water, busiest beaches, and highest demand for boat rentals. Book 48 hours ahead for popular boats and sunset slots.

June and September are ideal for boat rental — warm sea temperatures, lighter crowds, and more forgiving wind on north-coast days. May and October offer cooler water but excellent value and space at anchor.

Culture and history

Thassos was wealthy in antiquity thanks to marble, timber, and gold. The ancient quarry at Aliki — reachable by rental boat from Limenaria — exported columns across the Mediterranean. Submerged ruins are still visible to snorkellers from the boat ladder.

Traditional villages like Theologos and Kazaviti preserve stone architecture and mountain atmosphere inland. From the boat, you view coastal settlements like Potos and Aliki from the water while staying on board at anchor.

Marble and pine — the island's identity

Thassos white marble was famous throughout the ancient world — Marble Beach (Saliara) on the north shore shows raw scree tumbling into emerald water. Pine forests reach the shore in many bays, giving Thassos a scent and shade rare among Greek islands.

Respect protected archaeological zones at Aliki and coastal nature. Take all rubbish back to New Port of Limenaria after your rental day.

title: Palataki Limenaria — The Little Palace Landmark on Thassos
excerpt: History, views, and how to see Palataki — the neoclassical 'little palace' above Limenaria's old mining pier on Thassos, plus pairing the landmark with a self-drive boat rental from New Port of Limenaria.
content:
What is Palataki?

Palataki (Παλατάκι — 'little palace') is a striking neoclassical villa on a rocky cape above Limenaria's former iron-ore loading pier on Thassos' south coast. Built in the early 20th century for the Speidel mining company, it housed offices and guest quarters for German engineers overseeing ore exports from Metalia.

Today the ruin is one of Limenaria's most photographed landmarks — white columns and arched windows silhouetted against the Aegean. It is not a museum; respect fences and avoid climbing unstable masonry.

Seeing Palataki from land

From Limenaria town, follow the coastal path south toward the old pier. Golden-hour light (roughly 19:00–20:30 in summer) paints the facade warm orange. Allow 30–45 minutes for a walk-and-photo stop.

Pair the walk with dinner on the harbour promenade — many Rent A Boat Villy guests return from a boat rental, stroll to Palataki, then eat waterfront.

Mining heritage context

Thassos iron ore was loaded at this pier from nearby Metalia mines. The red-stained cliffs at Metalia Beach — your nearest snorkel stop by rental boat — come from the same geological story.

Understanding Palataki and Metalia together explains Limenaria's industrial past and turquoise present.

Palataki from the water

A self-drive rental from New Port of Limenaria lets you view Palataki from offshore while staying on board. Sunset boat rentals often anchor near Kalogria Bay with the landmark visible on the horizon.

Greece allows recreational self-drive boat rental on thousands of kilometres of coastline. Rules differ by horsepower, boat type, and company policy. Do you need a licence in Greece?

For boats up to 30 horsepower (30HP / 30PS), Greek law does not require a skipper licence for recreational rental. Most of our fleet at Limenaria qualifies — couples and families can drive themselves after briefing.

Larger engines or cabin cruisers above 30HP may require a valid licence or proof of experience. We confirm requirements per boat on boat fleet before you book online.

Minimum age and ID

Bring a valid passport or national ID. Minimum age rules apply and are confirmed at booking and marina check-in. Non-EU guests use passport; EU ID cards are accepted.
